title: Share Trading Policy

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: The Board; directors and company secretary of any subsidiary; any person entitled to receive equity performance rights and/or options under an equity incentive scheme; any Executives; and the Company Secretary. Subject to prohibited-period restrictions, dealing notification to the Company Secretary/Chairperson, Board-imposed embargoes, an absolute hedging ban, and a consent requirement for margin lending arrangements.

tiers.name: Directors, Executives and employees
tiers.description: All Directors, Executives and employees. Subject only to the Insider Trading Policy's prohibition on dealing while in possession of price sensitive information; the Share Trading Policy's prohibited periods, hedging ban and margin loan consent requirement do not extend to this tier unless the person is also a Restricted Person.

tiers.name: Associated Parties
tiers.description: Immediate family (including a spouse (or equivalent) or dependent), family company or trust of a Restricted Person. Each Restricted Person is personally responsible for ensuring associated parties comply with the same restrictions.

definitions.hedging_definition: Hedging arrangements include entering into transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding securities in the Company.

windows.start_anchor: 5 business days before the announcement of a dividend or any other capital management initiative that might have a material impact on the share price
windows.end_anchor: announcement of the dividend or capital management initiative

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board has an absolute discretion to place an embargo on Restricted Persons and/or employees and/or their associated parties trading in the Company's shares at any time, and may from time to time designate further prohibited periods; confidentiality of such embargoes is not addressed.

rules.detail: No separate derivatives rule exists. A purchased put or a collar over Company shares is a transaction in financial products that limits the economic risk of holding the shares, so it falls within the absolute hedging ban with no consent or clearance mechanism.
rules.evidence: Hedging arrangements include entering into transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding securities in the Company.

rules.detail: This tier is subject only to the Insider Trading Policy; no hedging or derivatives ban applies unless the person is also a Restricted Person.
rules.evidence: All Directors, Executives and employees must not deal in the Company's shares while in possession of price sensitive information.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on hedging arrangements over shares, options and rights in the Company, with no vesting distinction, no clearance route and no Company consent mechanism (unlike margin lending).
rules.evidence: A Restricted Person must not enter into hedging arrangements with respect to securities in the Company (including any shares, options and rights).

rules.detail: The hedging ban in section 1.10 is limited to Restricted Persons.

Not named. A monetisation structure (e.g. a prepaid forward) that limits the economic risk of holding Company shares falls within the hedging arrangement definition and is banned; an outright sale is unrestricted by this clause and instead subject to the notification rules.
rules.evidence: Hedging arrangements include entering into transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding securities in the Company.

rules.detail: Short selling is not named anywhere in the policy.
Securities lending is not named anywhere in the policy.
Not named. A CFD position over Company securities that limits the economic risk of a shareholding is a hedging arrangement and is banned.
rules.evidence: Hedging arrangements include entering into transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding securities in the Company.

rules.detail: Margin loans over Company securities require the Company's prior consent, which may be made subject to conditions; this is the only financing-type restriction with an available clearance route.
rules.evidence: A Restricted Person must not include his or her securities in the Company in a margin loan portfolio or otherwise deal in securities in the Company pursuant to a margin lending arrangement without first obtaining the Company's consent.

rules.detail: The margin lending consent requirement in section 1.11 is limited to Restricted Persons.

The only encumbrance addressed is via a margin lending arrangement (including transferring securities into an existing margin loan account), permitted only with prior Company consent, which may be conditional. General security interests unconnected to a margin loan are not addressed.
rules.evidence: entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of securities in the Company; transferring securities in the Company into an existing margin loan account

rules.detail: Only margin lending arrangements are addressed; broader secured financing not linked to a margin loan is not addressed. A margin loan secured on Company shares needs prior Company consent, which may be conditioned, for example on the circumstances in which shares may be sold to satisfy a margin call.
rules.evidence: A Restricted Person must not include his or her securities in the Company in a margin loan portfolio or otherwise deal in securities in the Company pursuant to a margin lending arrangement without first obtaining the Company's consent.

rules.detail: No short-term dealing or minimum holding period rule appears anywhere in the policy.

clearance.approver: Company Secretary, in conference with the Chairperson
clearance.evidence: Restricted Persons are required to notify the Company of intended dealings in the Company's shares, by themselves or their associated parties, prior to such intended dealings. ... The Chairperson and the Company Secretary must keep a written record of ... any clearance or refusal to grant clearance given under this Share Trading Policy.

exceptions.evidence: clearance may be given for the Restricted Person to sell (but not to purchase) shares in the Company when that person would otherwise be prohibited from doing so ... 'exceptional circumstances' means severe financial hardship
a court order (or court enforceable undertaking), or some other overriding legal or regulatory requirement, to transfer or sell shares in the Company
or other circumstances that may be deemed exceptional by the Chairperson.

an investment in, or trading in units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme only investing in the securities of the entity) where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party.
transfers of securities of the entity already held into a superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which the Restricted Person is a beneficiary

trading under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the security holders, such as, a rights issue, a security purchase plan, a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan and an equal access buy-back
the cancellation or surrender of an option under an employee scheme
undertakings to accept, or the acceptance of, a takeover offer or pursuant to a scheme of arrangement implemented in accordance with section 411 of the Corporations Act

financing.price_trigger_guidance: The Company may make any clearance granted for a margin lending arrangement conditional upon such terms and conditions as it sees fit, for example in regards to the circumstances in which the securities may be sold to satisfy a margin call.

exemption_authority: The Chairperson has sole discretion to determine whether circumstances are 'exceptional' and to grant written clearance (specifying its maximum duration) for a sale only, never a purchase, during an otherwise prohibited period; the Chairperson must refuse if there is a matter about which there is inside information in relation to Company shares at the time of the request.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Hedging arrangements include entering into transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding securities in the Company.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A purchased put, and the collar as a whole, squarely fits this definition, so the absolute hedging ban applies to Restricted Persons with no consent or clearance mechanism at all, unlike the margin loan provision.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Restricted Person must not include his or her securities in the Company in a margin loan portfolio or otherwise deal in securities in the Company pursuant to a margin lending arrangement without first obtaining the Company's consent.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg secured against Company shares is only conditionally restricted and can proceed with the Company's prior consent, potentially subject to conditions on forced-sale triggers, but this cannot cure the outright hedging prohibition on the derivative legs.

bespoke_clauses.clause: clearance may be given for the Restricted Person to sell (but not to purchase) shares in the Company when that person would otherwise be prohibited from doing so.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even in hardship, only a sale can be cleared during a prohibited period; delivering or physically settling shares under a collar during a prohibited period would need to fit within this narrow sale-only exception.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Chairperson must determine, and specify in the written clearance, the maximum duration of the clearance.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no default execution window; the collar's execution timetable (if it were otherwise permitted) would be entirely at the Chairperson's discretion.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Each Restricted Person has a personal responsibility to ensure that his or her 'associated parties' (being immediate family (including a spouse (or equivalent) or dependent), family company or trust) complies with the same respective restrictions as apply to Restricted Persons.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a spouse, family trust or family company does not escape the hedging ban or margin loan consent requirement.

summary: A funded collar is not achievable for Restricted Persons (the Board, subsidiary directors/company secretary, equity-incentive participants, Executives and the Company Secretary) under this policy. Section 1.10 imposes an absolute, unconditional ban on 'hedging arrangements', defined to include any transaction in financial products that limits the economic risk of holding Company securities, which squarely captures a purchased put or a full collar, and unlike the margin loan provision there is no consent, clearance or exemption mechanism available for it. The loan leg is only conditionally restricted: a margin loan or other margin lending arrangement secured on Company shares requires the Company's prior consent, which may be granted subject to conditions such as forced-sale triggers, but that permission cannot cure the outright prohibition on the derivative legs. Outside prohibited periods (5 business days before a dividend or capital management announcement, or a Board-imposed embargo) and while not holding inside information, an ordinary sale otherwise requires prior written notification to the Company Secretary and the Chairperson, and only a sale (never a purchase) can be cleared in exceptional circumstances (hardship, court order, or other Chairperson-approved cause) during a prohibited period. Restricted Persons' associated parties (spouse, dependants, family trust or company) are bound by the same hedging ban and margin loan consent requirement, so the structure cannot be routed around the policy through them.
